daysToHarvestRange.notes: Two Starke Ayres cultivars (Odyssey, Invictus) were verified as real, adapted SA cultivars, but their product pages did not state verifiable day-to-maturity figures reachable this session; two other product pages (Defender, Assegai) returned HTTP 500 errors, so WebSearch-reported maturity numbers for those (e.g. '90 days') could not be confirmed verbatim and are excluded.

yield.conditions: Conservative 7-8 t/ha, likely 10 t/ha, target 15 t/ha (KZN)

evidence.doc: KZN DARD, 'Expected Yields' (Vegetable Production series), Table 8

varieties.name: Odyssey
varieties.notes: Quoted verbatim: 'very well adapted for summer production and copes extremely well with hot and dry climates', plants described as prolific, 'often yielding two marketable ears per plant'. No verified day-count could be obtained this session.

varieties.name: Invictus
varieties.notes: Quoted verbatim: 'fast-maturing ... well adapted for summer and winter production.' No specific months or provinces stated, so no zone keys are assigned beyond noting its dual-season adaptability.

gaps: Winter/Western Cape sowing months not sourced: KZN DARD's calendar is KZN-specific, and while Starke Ayres states Invictus is 'well adapted for summer and winter production', it gives no explicit months or provinces for that winter window.

Seed rate note: KZN DARD's Table 5 adds 'Note: Super Sweet sweet-corn has a shrunken seed and would have nearly double the seed count per kg seed than that of standard sweet corn. Seeding rates are thus likely to be about half that shown above' (same doc, p7) — the seedRateKgPerHaRange given here (12-15kg/ha) is for standard (non-shrunken-seed) sweetcorn only.

Verified day-to-maturity figures for two commercially important Starke Ayres sweetcorn cultivars (Defender, Assegai) could not be obtained: both product pages returned HTTP 500 errors on direct fetch, so WebSearch-snippet-only maturity claims for them were excluded per the sourcing rules.
summary: Frost tenderness, transplant status, days-to-harvest, row/in-row spacing, seed rate and yield are all sourced from KZN DARD's Vegetable Production series (Tables 1/2, 4, 5, 6, 8). Verdict held to 'partial' because winter/Western Cape sowMonths could not be sourced with specific months.
